originalTitle: Why bond investors are pushing up some of your interest rates
summary: Many types of consumer loans such as mortgages peg their interest rate to the yield on 10-year Treasury bonds, which has been moving higher.
content:
The Federal Reserve sets national interest rate policy . But the U.S. central bank isn't the only major player in this arena: Bond investors also have a big influence on consumers' borrowing costs.

Many types of consumer loans — such as mortgages and auto loans — often peg their interest rates to 10-year U.S. Treasury bonds . That means their rates move higher when 10-year Treasury yields increase, and vice versa.

Those bond yields have increased steadily over the past several months.

The 10-year Treasury yield was about 4.7% as of market close on Thursday, its highest level since January 2025.

The rates on 30-year fixed mortgages on Thursday — about 6.6% — rose to their highest since August 2025, according to weekly data posted by Freddie Mac. Those on 15-year fixed-rate mortgages increased to about 6% this week, the highest since June 2025, Freddie Mac said.

Those price pressures come amid others for households, economists said.

Average gasoline prices topped $4 a gallon again this week amid renewed tensions in the Iran war, according to data from the Energy Information Administration.

The Trump administration also imposed a slew of new tariffs on dozens of countries on Friday. These import taxes raise costs for consumers and businesses, according to economists.

Read more CNBC personal finance coverage

Inflation across the U.S. economy has also been above policymakers' target for more than five years, and the financial cushion provided by relatively high tax refunds this spring appears to have waned, economists said.

The rise in Treasury yields is "just another drag for households when you've got affordability hits elsewhere," said Thomas Ryan, a North America economist at Capital Economics.

"And we don't see much relief in terms of the borrowing cost side of things," he said.

Why have Treasury yields increased?

The Fed sets an interest-rate benchmark known as the federal funds rate.

That benchmark has a direct impact on shorter-term interest rates, like those for credit cards and other variable-rate loans, said Chad NeSmith, a certified financial planner and director of investments at Tobias Financial Advisors, based in Plantation, Florida.

But bond investors tend to have a much greater influence over the movement of 10-year Treasury yields and those of other longer-term bonds.

More specifically, it's investors' expectations for future inflation and the trajectory of Fed interest rate policy that guide bond yields up or down, experts said.

For example, if bond investors expect inflation to move higher, they will demand a higher yield on longer-term Treasury bonds to compensate for the risk of inflation eroding their future returns, experts said.

"It's investors pricing their own reality, and that has a big knock-on effect on consumers in terms of what [rates] they can borrow at," Ryan said.

In this case, many factors are feeding into investor anxieties about inflation, such as oil prices , which jumped sharply in July as tensions in the Middle East have ratcheted upward.

Sustained high oil prices can filter through to prices across the U.S. economy, for things like airline tickets, transportation and goods, NeSmith said.

Capital Economics expects the Fed to raise interest rates three times this year, not necessarily in response to high oil prices but more so "a broader view that inflation looks hot," Ryan said.

Homeownership likely the biggest impact

Consumers will largely feel the impact of higher Treasury yields in their ability to buy or sell a home, NeSmith said.

Mortgage rates are more than double what they were during the Covid-19 pandemic, for example, and they could move above 7%, experts said.

"It will increase the lock-in effect in the housing market, where they feel trapped," NeSmith said.

Consumers who can't find an affordable rate for auto loans might forgo buying a new car, for example, he said.

"It just slows spending, because people have to borrow so much more," NeSmith said.
chineseTitle: 为什么债券投资者会推高部分利率
chineseSummary: 许多类型的消费贷款（例如抵押贷款）的利率与十年期国债的收益率挂钩，而十年期国债的收益率一直在走高。
chineseContent:
美联储制定国家利率政策。但美联储并不是这个领域的唯一主要参与者：债券投资者对消费者的借贷成本也有很大影响。

许多类型的消费贷款——例如抵押贷款和汽车贷款——通常将利率与十年期美国国债挂钩。这意味着当 10 年期国债收益率上升时，它们的利率就会上升，反之亦然。

这些债券的收益率在过去几个月中稳步上升。

截至周四收盘，10年期国债收益率约为4.7%，为2025年1月以来的最高水平。

根据房地美发布的每周数据，周四 30 年期固定抵押贷款利率（约 6.6%）升至 2025 年 8 月以来的最高水平。房地美表示，本周 15 年期固定利率抵押贷款利率增至 6% 左右，为 2025 年 6 月以来的最高水平。

经济学家表示，这些价格压力与家庭面临的其他压力不相上下。

根据能源情报署的数据，由于伊朗战争局势再度紧张，平均汽油价格本周再次突破每加仑 4 美元。

特朗普政府周五还对数十个国家征收了一系列新关税。经济学家表示，这些进口税增加了消费者和企业的成本。

阅读更多 CNBC 个人理财报道

经济学家表示，美国经济的通胀率五年多以来一直高于政策制定者的目标，而今年春季相对较高的退税所提供的财务缓冲似乎已经减弱。

凯投宏观(Capital Economics)北美经济学家托马斯·瑞安(Thomas Ryan)表示，国债收益率的上升“只是当其他地方的负担能力受到打击时对家庭的另一个拖累”。

“就借贷成本而言，我们并没有看到太大的缓解，”他说。

为何国债收益率上升？

美联储设定了一个称为联邦基金利率的利率基准。

位于佛罗里达州种植园的 Tobias Financial Advisors 的注册财务规划师兼投资总监查德·内史密斯 (Chad NeSmith) 表示，这一基准对短期利率有直接影响，例如信用卡和其他可变利率贷款的利率。

但债券投资者往往对10年期国债收益率和其他长期债券收益率的变动有更大的影响力。

专家表示，更具体地说，投资者对未来通胀的预期和美联储利率政策的轨迹引导着债券收益率的上升或下降。

例如，专家表示，如果债券投资者预计通胀率将走高，他们就会要求长期国债收益率提高，以弥补通胀侵蚀其未来回报的风险。

瑞安表示：“投资者对自己的现实情况进行定价，这对消费者的借贷利率产生了巨大的连锁反应。”

在这种情况下，许多因素加剧了投资者对通胀的担忧，例如随着中东紧张局势加剧，油价在 7 月份大幅上涨。

内史密斯表示，持续的高油价可能会影响整个美国经济的价格，例如机票、交通和商品等。

瑞安表示，凯投宏观预计美联储今年将加息三次，这不一定是为了应对高油价，更多的是“更广泛的观点认为通胀看起来很热”。

住房拥有率可能是最大的影响

内史密斯表示，消费者将在很大程度上感受到美国国债收益率上升对其购买或出售房屋能力的影响。

例如，专家表示，抵押贷款利率是 Covid-19 大流行期间的两倍多，并且可能会升至 7% 以上。

内史密斯说：“这将增加房地产市场的锁定效应，让他们感觉被困住了。”

他说，例如，无法找到负担得起的汽车贷款利率的消费者可能会放弃购买新车。

“这只会减缓支出，因为人们不得不借更多的钱，”内史密斯说。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
